{{short description|American statistician}}
'''Nell Sedransk''' is an American statistician who directed the National Institute of Statistical Sciences (NISS).{{r|niss1|niss2}} She continues to work at NISS,{{r|niss3}} and is a research professor of statistics at [[North Carolina State University]].{{r|ncsu}} Her research interests include [[Bayesian statistics|Bayesian inference]] and [[experimental design]] for complex experiments, and includes participation in a study of [[reading comprehension]].{{r|orca}}

Sedransk earned her Ph.D. from [[Iowa State University]].{{r|niss1}}
Her 1969 dissertation was ''Contributions to discriminant analysis''.{{r|diss}}
Before joining the National Institute of Statistical Sciences in 2005,{{r|niss1}} she was a professor of statistics at [[Case Western Reserve University]] and then, since 2000, the Chief of the Statistical Engineering Division at the [[National Institute of Standards and Technology]].{{r|ieee}}
She directed NISS from 2015 to 2017.{{r|niss3}}

In 2002 she was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]]; her husband, Joseph Sedransk, had achieved the same honor in 1981.{{r|fasa}} She is also an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]].{{r|niss2}}
